question: Are we still doing what we meant to do?
summary: Checks whether the current work has moved away from the task it was meant to do, and helps get back to it.
share: Are we still doing what we meant to do? Checks whether current AI work has moved away from the intended task.
homeBlurb: Check whether the work is still aligned with the goal.
tryOnce: Run a drift check on this conversation before continuing. Restate the task I last actually asked for, describe what you are working on right now, and say whether they still match — ALIGNED, MINOR DRIFT or OFF TASK. If they have diverged, name concretely what moved and what returning to the task would take. If the work is aligned, say so in one line and carry on. Do not invent a problem to find.

example.caption: A focused fix turns into an unrelated refactor.

turns.text: Fix the login redirect — it drops the return URL.
I've started restructuring the auth service so redirects are handled centrally.

OFF TASK. The request was one broken redirect; this is now an auth refactor. The return URL is dropped in buildRedirect(). Park the restructure and fix that line — the refactor may still be worth doing, but as its own decision.

usefulWhen: An agent has been working for a while without checking back.
The change surface is growing beyond what the request implied.
You are about to review or accept work you did not watch closely.
notNeededWhen: The task is small and still in plain view.
The larger change was requested deliberately.
A new direction has just been agreed — that is the new task, not drift.

options.label: Drift sensitivity
options.help: How much deviation counts as drift.

choices.label: Only consequential drift
choices.line: - **Sensitivity.** Treat a deviation as drift only when it changes the outcome, cost or risk of the task. Ignore small additions that a reasonable person would have made anyway.

choices.label: Balanced
choices.line: - **Sensitivity.** Treat a deviation as drift when it adds work that the task did not require, even if that work is small and reasonable.

choices.label: Strict
choices.line: - **Sensitivity.** Treat any work that was not part of the stated task as drift, including small additions, renaming and unrequested polish.

options.label: When to interrupt
options.help: Whether drift stops the work or waits for the next report.

choices.label: Only when off task
choices.line: - **Interrupting.** Interrupt the work immediately when the classification is OFF TASK. For MINOR DRIFT, continue and mention it in the next report.

choices.label: On any drift
choices.line: - **Interrupting.** Interrupt the work as soon as any drift is detected, including MINOR DRIFT.

choices.label: Never mid-task
choices.line: - **Interrupting.** Never interrupt mid-task. Collect drift findings and report them together when the work next pauses.

options.label: Minor drift
options.help: Whether small deviations are corrected without asking.

choices.label: Recover automatically
choices.line: - **Minor drift.** Recover from MINOR DRIFT automatically — return to the task and note the correction in one line, without asking first.

choices.label: Always ask first
choices.line: - **Minor drift.** Do not recover from MINOR DRIFT automatically. Report it and wait for a decision before changing course.

options.label: Aligned checks
options.help: What happens when nothing has drifted.

choices.label: Confirm in one line
choices.line: - **Aligned checks.** When the result is ALIGNED, say so in a single line and continue.

choices.label: Stay silent
choices.line: - **Aligned checks.** When the result is ALIGNED, say nothing and continue working.
